facts.statement: Sphagesaurus was an extinct notosuchian crocodylomorph belonging to the family Sphagesauridae.
facts.quote: Sphagesaurus is an extinct genus of sphagesaurid notosuchian crocodylomorph from the Late Cretaceous of southwest São Paulo, southern Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus Sphagesaurus and its type species S. huenei were first described by Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1950.
facts.quote: Sphagesaurus was first described and named by Llewellyn Ivor Price in 1950 and the type species is S. huenei.

facts.statement: The original description of S. huenei was based on two isolated molariform maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: S. huenei was described by Price (1950) on the basis of two isolated molariform maxillary teeth

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of S. huenei was discovered in a railway cut between Presidente Bernardes and Santo Anastácio in São Paulo state.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in a railway cut between the cities of Presidente Bernardes and Santo Anastacio in the state of São Paulo

facts.statement: The referred specimen DGM 333-R was found near Catanduva in São Paulo state within the Bauru Group.
facts.quote: DGM 333-R was found near Catanduva city of São Paulo, both from the Bauru Group.

facts.statement: A second species, S. montealtensis, was named by Andrade and Bertini in 2008 based on a nearly complete skull and mandible.
facts.quote: A second species, S. montealtensis, was described from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil. It was named by Marco Brandalise de Andrade and Reinaldo J. Bertini in 2008

facts.statement: In 2013, the species S. montealtensis was reassigned to the genus Caipirasuchus, becoming Caipirasuchus montealtensis.
facts.quote: In 2013, this specimen was reassigned to the closely related notosuchian genus Caipirasuchus, creating the combinatio nova Caipirasuchus montealtensis.

facts.statement: Sphagesaurus is classified within the family Sphagesauridae.
The authority for the genus name Sphagesaurus is Price, 1950.
Sphagesaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from approximately 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2026, Kitayama and Bertini provisionally proposed that Armadillosuchus arrudai and Caryonosuchus pricei are junior synonyms of S. huenei.
facts.quote: In a 2026 taxonomic review, Pedro Akira Kitayama and Reinaldo José Bertini proposed that Armadillosuchus arrudai and Caryonosuchus pricei were junior synonyms of S. huenei, explicitly treating this interpretation as provisional.

facts.statement: Kitayama and Bertini (2026) reviewed a skull with mandibular and postcranial remains as comparative material for S. huenei.
facts.quote: Kitayama and Bertini (2026) also reviewed URC-R-92, a skull with mandibular and postcranial remains previously reported in 2006 and described in 2009, as comparative material of S. huenei.

facts.statement: Bertini et al. (1993) referred an isolated molariform tooth from the Adamantina Formation to S. huenei.
facts.quote: Bertini et al. (1993) referred the isolated molariform tooth, URC-R 015 from Locality 99 of the Adamantina Formation, to S. huenei

facts.statement: The holotype of S. montealtensis was collected from the Bairro Cachoeira locality near Monte Alto in northern São Paulo from the Adamantina Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Bairro Cachoeira locality at the base of the Serra da Água Limpa, about 8 km northwest of Monte Alto city of northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.

facts.statement: A nearly complete cranium, mandible, and posterior postcranium referred to the Caipirasuchus lineage was discovered in Catanduva, northern São Paulo.
facts.quote: MPMA 68-0003/12 consists of a nearly complete cranium and mandible and a posterior portion of the postcranium. It was discovered in the municipality of Catanduva, northern São Paulo, from the Adamantina Formation.

rejected.quote: Kellner et al. (2011) reassigned DGM 1411-R, a nearly complete but crushed anterior portion of the skull and lower jaw, to a new genus and species, Caryonosuchus pricei.
